title: Compact parametrix and one-sided invertibility for mirror quantum two-sphere Dirac-type gluing with summable Fourier weights and uniformly nonzero Jacobi coefficient products
author: Slawomir Klimek; Matt McBride
work: A Note on Gluing Dirac Type Operators on a Mirror Quantum Two-Sphere
source_version: Official SIGMA 10 (2014) article 036, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2014.036; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof solves every coupled boundary Fourier mode and constructs three infinite-series inverse kernels with the required boundary matching. Uniform product bounds and the weight-sum hypotheses give Hilbert-Schmidt control whose norms vanish with mode number, producing a compact global parametrix and an explicit finite-rank left defect.

source_check.note: The full original quantum compact-parametrix Theorem 3.6 is retained with every new Jacobi kernel/inverse, boundary-limit, coupled Fourier-mode matching, explicit three inverse kernels, global parametrix and Hilbert-Schmidt estimate proof, including the supporting author classical gluing argument to which the final closure refers. All weight summability, vanishing mode sums, uniformly bounded a/b-squared sums, nonzero product bounds and full reciprocal-product limits are preserved. The exact positive/negative Fourier boundary exchange and zeroth matching are retained; DQ=Id and the finite-rank left defect are the source outcome. Routine displayed-kernel substitutions remain the author checks. No generic-weight extension, self-adjointness, spectral-triple claim or special q-weight example is selected. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Complete Theorem3.6 proof chain, Jacobi kernel and inverse equations, boundary limits, global parametrix Proposition3.11 and Hilbert-Schmidt Proposition3.12 read. The Hilbert norm uses the displayed mode-dependent weights a^(n); positive a,b satisfy sum1/a=s(n) finite with s(n)->0 and sum a/b-squared=t(n) uniformly bounded. Products of c-plus/c-minus are uniformly between kappa and kappa inverse, and each full reciprocal product exists. Exact positive/negative Fourier boundary exchange and zeroth coefficient matching are retained. The inverse has DQ=Id,QD=Id-C with explicit rank-one C. Repeated inverse substitutions are source-author routine checks after the kernels are displayed, not omitted construction. No self-adjoint spectral-triple assertion or special q-weight example is selected.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem3.6 for D(f,g)=(delta f,delta g) of(3.3)-(3.4) on H1 directsum H1 with the Section3 coefficient hypotheses and boundary f_n-plus(infinity)=g_n-minus(infinity),f_n-minus=g_n-plus for n>=1 and matching zeroth plus coefficients. D has a right inverse and is left invertible modulo compacts, with compact parametrix. No generic weights, arbitrary boundary condition or self-adjointness claim.

The selected construction uses those displayed operator domains and preserves the original author pages.
